expectations.text: No claim is inflated: the figure of four hundred signups is not rounded up, no new absolute or superlative is added, and 'a lesson I keep having to relearn' is not turned into a promise
expectations.evidence: 'About four hundred' is preserved with its hedge, and the lesson is not turned into a promise. But the rewrite replaces 'a lesson I keep having to relearn' with 'it taught me, again, that a test team can only catch the mistakes it knows how to make', which adds a new categorical absolute ('can only') stated as a general truth about all test teams. The author made no such claim. The executor's own user_notes concede this: 'a grader may consider adding a claim the author did not make to be overreach.' The response also changes 'It cost us' to 'The bug cost us', narrowing the referent, which the executor also flagged.

expectations.text: If a figure is applied, the response names it and the trigger condition that licensed it; if none is applied, the response says so and explains why the paragraph already lands
expectations.evidence: Neither branch is satisfied. It also does not declare that no figure was applied; instead it says the paragraph is 'already in good shape' and then rewrites three sentences, including the ending it calls 'a blank'. The 'Things I left alone on purpose' list explains what was kept, not why the paragraph already lands without changes.

suggestions.assertion: No claim is inflated: the figure of four hundred signups is not rounded up, no new absolute or superlative is added, and 'a lesson I keep having to relearn' is not turned into a promise
suggestions.reason: The failure mode this arm actually exhibited, restating an implicit lesson as an explicit general maxim, is only caught here because the maxim happens to contain 'only'. A version of the maxim without an absolute ('a test team tends to catch the mistakes it knows how to make') would pass all three sub-clauses while still putting words in the author's mouth. Consider adding 'and no lesson or takeaway is stated that the author left implicit'.

No assertion checks whether the closing sentence was preserved or whether non-figure structural edits (sentence splits, subject swaps) were made. For an eval named 'already-good-restraint', the most discriminating check is whether the executor recognized the existing zeugma at the ending and left it alone. Expectation 2 passed here despite the ending being rewritten.
scan.txt flagged 'here is a' as a sycophancy pattern in the response's framing prose. Not a graded outcome, but worth noting that the baseline framing tripped a surface flag the skilled arm did not.

eval_feedback.overall: The baseline preserved every concrete detail but did not state a budget, did not name the figure it sharpened or a trigger for it, and rewrote the understated ending into a categorical maxim the author never made. The assertions caught this, but partly by luck of wording; a direct check on the closing sentence would make the eval more robust.
